findings.title: Table widget renders hardcoded empty data behind feature flag
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the organization has the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag, the new `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}` instead of the actual `tableResults`, `fields`, `eventView`, and `location` that the existing `StyledSimpleTableChart` uses. Any org enrolled in the flag will see a completely empty dashboard table (no rows, no columns) regardless of the query results. This looks like placeholder/wiring code that was merged prematurely; the real data is never passed to the new component.

findings.title: fetch_error_details misaligns error IDs with nodestore data via zip on dict values
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, then zips `error_ids` with `events.values()`. `get_multi` returns a dict, and per its contract keys with no result may be absent from the dict. When any node is missing (or dict ordering differs from insertion order), `zip` pairs the wrong `event_id` with the wrong `data`, producing ErrorEvents whose id/title/message/timestamp belong to a different error. It should iterate the returned mapping by node_id (e.g. `zip(node_ids, (events.get(n) for n in node_ids))`) and skip None values, so each event_id maps to its own node data.

findings.title: query() mutates the caller's selected_columns list
findings.body: In `ourlogs.query`, when ordering by timestamp the function appends `tags[sentry.timestamp_precise,number]` directly to the `selected_columns` argument (`selected_columns.append(precise_timestamp)`). This mutates a list owned by the caller. If the same list object is reused across calls (common when a request handler builds fields once and retries, or caches them), the precise-timestamp column is appended repeatedly and leaks into responses/other query paths, potentially causing duplicate columns or unexpected `field` validation errors. The function should copy the list (`selected_columns = [*selected_columns, precise_timestamp]`) before appending.

findings.title: Frontend queries /organizations/<slug>/feedback-summary/ endpoint that has no backend in this PR
findings.body: The new `useFeedbackSummary` hook (and the `FeedbackSummary` component rendered on the feedback list page) issues GET requests to `/organizations/${organization.slug}/feedback-summary/`. No such endpoint, URL registration, or handler appears anywhere in this pull request, so for any organization with the `user-feedback-ai-summaries` feature flag enabled, the feedback list page will fire a request that 404s on every load. Either the backend endpoint needs to be part of this change or the hook/component must not ship enabled.

findings.title: ErrorEvent title/message read keys that raw nodestore payloads don't contain
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` reads `data.get("title", "")` and `data.get("message", "")` from raw nodestore event payloads. Raw event data stored in nodestore contains structured entries (e.g. `exception.values[].type/value`), not precomputed `title`/`message` fields, so the generated error log messages (`generate_error_log_message`) will typically render as `User experienced an error: ': ' at <timestamp>` with no error type or message, defeating the purpose of including error context in the Seer summary prompt. The fields should be derived (e.g. from the exception entry) via the event model rather than read directly from the node dict.

findings.title: timestamp/age mutual-exclusion validation is bypassed for falsy values
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` checks `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` checks `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`, so the exclusion only triggers when the value is truthy. A report with `age: 0` plus a `timestamp`, or `timestamp: 0` plus an `age`, passes validation even though the specs require the two fields to be mutually exclusive. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` / `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` instead of truthiness checks.
